MARKETS.

MANCHESTER TRADE, FRIDAY. There is no improve- ment in this market, though, as is usual on Thursdays rather more inquiry is reported. Cotton is tamer somewhat, the day's business being covered by an estimate of 8,000 bales, and the prices are lower all round. Yarns are not active, but prices give way very slowly, consequently manufacturers leave them alone as much as possible. More enquiry for Calcutta and Bombay is on the market, but not much has been found workable. China buyers are doing very little, for Egypt and the Levant business is doing in small or moderate parcels, and buyers fight hard for concessions. Mr. Slater Lewis, Cheshire county councillor: addressing his constituents in Frodsham on Thus! day night, made reference to the recent coun4 police inquiry, of which he was the instigator. , asserted that upon the finding of the Corainiqee nearly 16 per cent, of the whole force in Cheshire, were drunken and reliable men. The Committee.% Inquiry, he complained, had in the case of tP.,, watching for game at Norton acted upon hears% statements and not upon evidence. Anyone knew anything about country life knew that pOll5, men had been gamekeepers in uniform for gelle'-‘ doss. If the Chief Constable (Colonel HaniersleY had scanned his men's journals he would have £001:1.9 that every constable under his autocratic wing busy watching for poachers every night fr0n11"1, Ist September. In conclusion F.: submitted that the Committee had found for hil'a (Mr. Lewis) on five-sixths of the report, that grill:, irregularities had taken place among Runecn„ police, that policemen had been watching poachers on private lands, and that. a fund for re- warding policemen for game preservation had been in existence at Macclesfield. Olizfshire, Merionethshire, Flintshire, Denbighshire, Caruarvonshire, and the Isle of Man, the license under patents for the selling and letting on hire the various machines for manufacturing and supplying either in bottles, or by a counter fountain on draught, high-class Mineral Waters of every kind (pure, or flavoured with varieties of syrup and essence) aerated with Liquefied Natural Carbonic Acid Gas. In quality, purity, and aeration, the Artificial Mineral Waters manufactured under these patents approach more nearly to Nature's standard—i.e., to Natural Mineral Waters—than any Artificial Waters produced until ' the Volcanic-Aeration Company (Limited) introduced the process. On the contrary. Liquefied Natural Carbonic Acid Gas' produces an aeration, which is absolutely free from all impu- rities, which is brisk, refreshing, and, for quenching thirst, unapproachable by any Water aerated with Artificial Gas. The price at which waters aerated with Liquefied Natural Gas, in all respects approaching the absolute perfection of Natural Mineral Waters (which are imported and retailed at very high prices in this country, can be manufactured in less than the price at which the common Artifical Mineral Waters are produced here. It can be produced at a cost of less than one penny per dozen. Owing to the small space (3ft. by lft. 61n.) required for working the machines, this system is especially suitable for use on board ship. Besides the better quality and cheaper price of the waters produced. a great saving would be effected in the freightage and storage of bottles, cases, &c., and in avoiding breakage and damage to same. The bursting of bottles also while being opened, a constant source of danger, andone from which serious accidents to the face and hands of the operator frequently occur, can be entirely obviated by the adoption of this system. Messrs. Spiers and Pond, the " Bodega " Company and others are using the Machines at their principal Refreshment Bars and Restaurants, in London and elsewhere. The Machines are now rented by a large number of the lead- ing Licensed Victuallers, Restaurateurs, &c., throughout the United Kingdom, and continue to give every satisfaction. As an evidence of the popularity which these Machines have attained, it is only necessary to state that Messrs. Spiers and Pond have fitted the Refreshment Bars at the Royal Military Exhibition, Chelsea, the great exhibition of the pre- sent season, exclusively with the Company's apparatus. Estimated income per annum to the Company from the rental and subsequent working of each set of apparatus for serving the Aerated Water an draught If fixed in a house, selling, say, three gross of Minerals per week, viz., two gross of plain sodas and one gross lemonade £l4 7s. 6d. and a net gain to the retailer of 17s. id. per week, after paying rental of apparatus, in favour of the Company's new system, or an annual net gain of £44 Bs. 4d. to the retailer, solely on the first cost of aerated drinks to him. The number of licensed houses of all kinds in the counties of Lancashire, Cheshire, and North Wales, including Liver- pool. Manchester, and Chester, by far exceeds 20,000, Lan- cashire alone contributing 17,131. This large aggregate does not include the numerous temperance refreshment rooms in the various districts reserved to this Company.. If only 4,000 machines be fitted up, and, basing the calcula- tion on the lowest computation of a honse selling only one i 1 gross per week, the income accruing to this Company would l be as follows : £45,800 Thus, after allowing 50 per cent, of the income for working expenses, depreciation of plant, &e., there would remain suf- ficient to pay over 20 per cent, dividend on the nominal capi- tal of the Company. In calculating the above estimate, the business to be done with Steamship Companies has not been taken into account, and, considering, the ever-increasing. passenger traffic arriving, and leaving the Port Of Liverpool, it is anticipated that this branch alone will produce a very large revenue. Copies of the Memorandum and Articles of Association may 'be inspected at, and Prospectuses and Forms of Application can be obtained, from the Bankers, Solicitors, Brokers, and at the Offices of the Company. November 6th. 1890.

FAIRFIELD WARD ELECTION. I beg to tender to the 330 Electors who recorded their votes ir.,my favour, my sincerest thanks for their support and con- fidence. I wish also to publicly acknowledge my great indebtedness to the number of generous and (indefatigable friends who worked so earnestly and heartily on my behalf. The minority of 5 was owing to no lack of effort on their part or mine, bet simply to the influence of my opponent and his friends with the workmen of the large Firm where he was formerly employed. I feel the result keenly,because of the disappointment to my supporters and the loss tothe Party, but the contest has been fairly fought, and will always be fraught in my mind with pleasant recollections of the great kindness and courtesy extended to me by the burgesses and others with whom the Election brought me into contact. HENRY JOHNSON LONGTON.

A SIX PER CENT. BANK RATE. The Bank-rate of discount has been raised to-day from five to six per cent. FURIOUS STORM. WRECKS AND CASUALTIES. Telegrams received indicate the great severity of Thursday night's gale. The bargue Kishon, of Appledore, went ashore early on Friday morning at I:Sude, the crew being rescued by the rocket apparatus. ' A vessel went ashore at Ilfracombe, and the Ilfra- combe Grand Hotel and other buildings in the town were much damaged. The schooner Ellen Beatrice, of Pembrey, was totally wrecked on Friday morning, while making for Working- ton. The crew were saved. The smack Wonder, of Whitehaven, sank in the storm, but thp crew were saved. Lloyd's agency reports the following casualties :—The brigantine Flora Ross, from London for Leith, has stranded on Ross sands; the four-masted ship County of Peebles, from Tysil for San Francisco, is ashore at Stan- nergate ; the ketch Vacuna, from London, is ashore at the outer banks of the river Humber, and the yacht : Urania has been wrecked at Bangor, County Cork. The owner of the last-named vessel was drowned. FATAL ACCIDENT AT ST. HELENS. A man named Thomas Erlam was killed at St. Helens, on Friday morning, owing to the fall, during the height of the gale, of a high chimney at the Ravenhead works of the London and Manchester Plateglass Company. A SCOTTISH NOBLEMAN DROWNED. A fierce easterly gale blew all last night on the north- east coast, accompanied by blinding sleet and rain. Word has just arrived of the wreck of a large yacht in Bognor Bay, the owner, who is a Scottish nobleman, be- ing drowned. WARRINGTON. Chimneys and roofs of buildings in all parts of the town have been damaged, and several hoardings, including the large advertisement hoarding in Scotland- road have been overthrown. WIDNES AND RUNCORN. Yesterday numerous slates were dislodged from roofs and chimney pots throw down, but there were no acci- dents of a serious character occurred. The river traffic was at a standstill. TERRIBLE EXPLOSION IN CHINA. THREE HUNDRED KILLED. SHANGHAI, FRIDAY.—The Government powder mills at Taiping Fu have been blown up. Three hundred persons were killed by the explosion.
